parts:
I am trying to learn lavaan and have started by trying to reproduce the small sample example in Tabachnick and Fidell (pg 692)
 
I have managed to get results, but they don't match up with the results the text reports for EQS or LISREL so I am pretty sure I am misunderstanding something.
 
Here is what I have so far:
 
# begin by entering the lower diagonal
# covariance matrix from page 629
 
lower <- '
  1.00
  .70  11.47
  .62  .62  1.87
  .44  .44  .95  1.17
  .30  .21  .54  .38  1.00'
 
TandFex.cov <-
  getCov(lower, names=c("NUMYEARS","DAYSKI",
                        "SNOWSAT","FOODSAT","SENSEEK"))
 
#recreate the model used by Tabachnick and Fidell
 
TandFex.model <-'
 
# latent variable definitions
  LOVESKI =~ NA*NUMYEARS + DAYSKI
  SKISAT =~ 1*SNOWSAT + FOODSAT
 
# regressions
  SKISAT ~ LOVESKI + SENSEEK
 
# variances and covariances

  NUMYEARS ~~ NUMYEARS
  DAYSKI ~~ DAYSKI
  FOODSAT ~~ FOODSAT
  SNOWSAT ~~ SNOWSAT
  SKISAT ~~ SKISAT'

 
fit <- lavaan(TandFex.model,
           sample.cov = TandFex.cov,
           sample.nobs = 5)
 
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)
Pointers would be greatly appreciated.
 
Michael

messages.subject: RE: Recreating small sample example from Tabachnick and Fidell
parts:
Michael—

 

In these lines:

# latent variable definitions
  LOVESKI =~ NA*NUMYEARS + DAYSKI
  SKISAT =~ 1*SNOWSAT + FOODSAT

You fixed the loading for SNOWSAT to 1 (setting the scale of the factor SKISAT), but you explicitly left the loading for NUMYEARS free.  You will need to set the scale for LOVESKI somehow, either by fixing a loading (to 1, say) or by fixing the variance of LOVESKI (say, at 1).  The lavaan function in the lavaan package will not do that by default.  Later in the code you explicitly free SKISAT’s variance:

 

  SKISAT ~~ SKISAT

 

     Is the number of observations really only 5?

 

           sample.nobs = 5)

 

If you try to estimate more free parameters than you have observations, thing probably will not go well.

 

--Ed Rigdon

On 04/17/2014 07:01 PM, Michael Granaas wrote:
> I am trying to learn lavaan and have started by trying to reproduce the
> small sample example in Tabachnick and Fidell (pg 692)

Is this what you need? (I have no access to the book, so I can not
compare the output).

TandFex.model <- '

# latent variable definitions
LOVESKI =~ NA*NUMYEARS + DAYSKI
SKISAT =~ 1*SNOWSAT + FOODSAT

# regressions
SKISAT ~ LOVESKI + SENSEEK
# residual variances observed

NUMYEARS ~~ NUMYEARS
DAYSKI ~~ DAYSKI
FOODSAT ~~ FOODSAT
SNOWSAT ~~ SNOWSAT

# (residual) variances latent

LOVESKI ~~ 1*LOVESKI

SKISAT ~~ SKISAT
'

fit <- lavaan(TandFex.model,
sample.cov = TandFex.cov,

sample.nobs = 5,
mimic = "EQS")


Alternative 1 (using auto.var=TRUE):

TandFex.model <- '

# latent variable definitions
LOVESKI =~ NA*NUMYEARS + DAYSKI
SKISAT =~ 1*SNOWSAT + FOODSAT

# regressions
SKISAT ~ LOVESKI + SENSEEK

# non-free (residual) variances

LOVESKI ~~ 1*LOVESKI

'

fit2 <- lavaan(TandFex.model,
sample.cov = TandFex.cov,
sample.nobs = 5,
auto.var = TRUE,
mimic = "EQS")


Alternative 2 (using the sem() function):

TandFex.model <- '

# latent variable definitions
LOVESKI =~ NA*NUMYEARS + DAYSKI
SKISAT =~ SNOWSAT + FOODSAT

# regressions
SKISAT ~ LOVESKI + SENSEEK

# non-free (residual) variances

LOVESKI ~~ 1*LOVESKI
'

fit3 <- sem(TandFex.model,
sample.cov = TandFex.cov,
sample.nobs = 5,
mimic = "EQS")


Yves.

parts:
I found the book, and it turns out that the sample size is N=100 (and not N=5). So for future reference, this syntax will replicate the output of Tabachnick & Fidell, rather nicely:

library(lavaan)
lower <- '
 1.000
 0.700  11.470
 0.623   0.623  1.874
 0.436   0.436  0.950  1.173
 0.300   0.210  0.540  0.380  1.00'

Table14.4 <- getCov(lower, names=c("NUMYEARS","DAYSKI",
"SNOWSAT","FOODSAT","SENSEEK"))

model <- '

# latent variable definitions
  LOVESKI =~ NA*NUMYEARS + DAYSKI
  SKISAT  =~ 1*SNOWSAT + FOODSAT
 
# regressions
  SKISAT ~ LOVESKI + SENSEEK

# (residual) variances latent
  LOVESKI ~~ 1*LOVESKI

'
 
fit <- sem(model, sample.cov = Table14.4, sample.nobs = 100, mimic="EQS")
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

On 04/18/2014 05:55 PM, Michael Granaas wrote:
> When I leave in the syntax:
>
> NUMYEARS ~~ NUMYEARS
> DAYSKI ~~ DAYSKI
> FOODSAT ~~ FOODSAT
> SNOWSAT ~~ SNOWSAT
>
> I seem to get the same answers using "sem" but not using "lavaan"
>
> My working hypothesis is that in "sem" I have simply duplicated the
> default settings, but that lavaan has fewer defaults and so I would need
> to include additional equations??

The sem() function is a 'user-friendly' function where a lot of default
settings keep the syntax compact.

The lavaan() function does not do anything automatically, so you need to
either specify all the parameters yourself, or you can add 'sets' of
parameters (eg variances) by using the auto.* flags.

This is all explained in the lavaan paper.

Yves.
